name: Chromatic segment (x cell)
use: Small chromatic cells. The fugue subject of Music for Strings uses all semitones from A to E

name: Whole-tone scale
use: Vagrant chords in Schoenberg. First movement of Bartók's String Quartet No. 4

name: Octatonic scale (semitone first)
use: A subset scale of the chromatic scale in the quartets. One octatonic scale = two axes of the axis system

name: Octatonic scale (whole tone first)
use: Same scale from its second note

name: Acoustic scale (Lydian with minor seventh)
use: From the overtone series. Finale of the Concerto for Orchestra. Mode 4 of the melodic minor scale

name: Dorian mode
use: The flute melody of The Night's Music (on C-sharp)

name: Phrygian mode
use: Half of the Phrygian-Lydian polymode. Also the cadence mode of Andalusian music

name: Lydian mode
use: Half of the Phrygian-Lydian polymode

name: Phrygian-Lydian polymode
use: Two modes on one tonic. All 12 notes, but with a tonic

name: Model 1:3
use: Minor third and semitone in alternation. It has the major and minor third and the major and minor sixth

name: Pentatonic scale without semitones (minor form)
use: Old-style Hungarian peasant song. Melody in the Mist: G A C D F

name: Pentatonic scale without semitones (major form)
use: End of the slow movement of Bartók's Piano Concerto No. 3

name: Fourths stack
use: Motto theme and chords of the Chamber Symphony No. 1

name: Minor scale with raised 4 and 7 (Hungarian minor)
use: Verbunkos style. Two augmented seconds

name: Phrygian with major third (Hijaz type)
use: One augmented second between steps 2 and 3

name: Maqam Rast
use: Neutral third and neutral seventh (between major and minor). Values are the 24-tone approximation

name: Maqam Bayati
use: Neutral second. A common maqam for song and for the call to prayer

name: Maqam Saba
use: Neutral second and lowered fourth. The top note is lower than the octave. Mood: grief. In the Turkish tradition, the maqam of the dawn call to prayer

name: Maqam Hijaz
use: Augmented second in the lower part. Real tuning makes the step smaller than 300 cents

name: Raga Yaman
use: First quarter of the night. Same notes as the Lydian mode. Main note: step 3. Second main note: step 7. Steps 1 and 5 are weak in the ascent. Typical phrase (steps): low 7, 2, 3, 2, 1; 5, raised 4, 3, 2, 1

name: Raga Bageshri
use: Middle of the night. Main note: step 4. Second main note: step 1. The ascent has no step 2 and no step 5 (five notes up, seven notes down)

name: Raga Malkauns
use: Late night, 24:00 to 03:00. No step 2 and no step 5. Main note: step 4. Second main note: step 1. Serious and meditative; low octave; slow tempo. Slides and a slow oscillation on the minor third and the minor sixth. Typical phrase (steps): 3, 4, 6, 4, 3, 4, 3, 1

name: Raga Darbari Kanada
use: Midnight, deep in the night. A grave raga, mostly in the low octave. Main note: step 2. Second main note: step 5. Slow slides, and a slow oscillation on the minor third. The line stays for some time on the low minor sixth

name: Slendro
use: Five pitches at almost equal distances in the octave. Each gamelan has its own tuning. The values are the equal-step model

name: Pelog
use: Seven unequal steps; the music uses five of them at a time. Each gamelan has its own tuning. The values are 7 of the 9 steps of an equal scale of 9 notes (measurement of 27 gamelans by Surjodiningrat, 1972)

name: In scale (miyako-bushi)
use: Koto and shamisen music. Semitones above steps 1 and 5

name: Yo scale
use: Folk song and shakuhachi music. No semitones
